# team-comms.md template

Scout writes `.agents/team-comms.md` during project seeding. One template
serves every host: dispatch works the same way everywhere — one call to the
host's subagent tool, by roster name — so the only host-specific content is
the § Setup line and the agent directory the roster was read from.

**Every generated `team-comms.md` must start with this header:**

```markdown
<!-- GENERATED BY SCOUT — DO NOT EDIT. Re-run scout to refresh. -->
```

The header is load-bearing: it tells readers (and future scout runs) that
the file is owned by the seeder and overwritten on every seed. Hand edits
will be lost.

Fill in: every detected host in § Setup (a project may have several), the
roster from the agent directories (one row per installed persona, including
co-installed factories' — e.g. manual-qa's `test-runner`), and the date.

---

## The template

```markdown
<!-- GENERATED BY SCOUT — DO NOT EDIT. Re-run scout to refresh. -->

# Team Communication

> Generated by scout on <YYYY-MM-DD>.

## Setup

- **Host(s):** <Claude Code (`.claude/agents/`) | GitHub Copilot (`.github/agents/`) | Cursor (`.cursor/agents/`) | … — list every one installed>
- **Dispatch:** one call to your host's subagent tool, by roster name. Prose never dispatches.
- **Installed personas:** <N> — see the roster below.

## Team roster

| Role | Agent name | Hand off… |
|------|------------|-----------|
<!-- one row per installed persona, from the agent file's frontmatter `name:` + `description` — the name is identical on every host; co-installed factories' personas get rows too -->
| Test Automation Lead (orchestrator) | `test-automation-lead` | Pipeline routing, dispatch, merge |
| Test Automation Engineer | `test-automation-engineer` | Automation implementation; the reviewer slot as a fresh dispatch |
| Scout | `scout` | Codebase onboarding, re-discovery |

Use the agent name exactly as the frontmatter spells it — it is the
directory name under `.claude/agents/`, the file name under
`.github/agents/`, and the value your subagent tool takes.

## How to hand off work

Dispatch is **one call to your host's subagent tool** — the tool in your list
that launches a named agent with a prompt. Pass the roster name exactly, a
3–5-word description, and a self-contained prompt. The call blocks; the
subagent's final message comes back as the tool result in the same turn.
There is no queue, no background mode and no notification.

**Always pass the agent's name**, even where the tool's schema marks it
optional: an unnamed call spawns a copy of the caller (or a generic agent),
not the persona you meant. **No subagent tool in your tool list at all** →
say so to the user and stop; never do the delegated work yourself instead.

Two things never dispatch: prose ("use the engineer agent to …" — the runtime
does not read your reply for instructions) and a call written as text in some
other host's syntax. Nothing needs enabling in any agent file: never add
`tools:` or `agents:` to make dispatch work.

**One subagent** — one call. **Several** — several calls in the same reply,
only for read-only work on a finished diff (reviewers); nothing that writes
runs concurrently, one working tree has one state at a time.

## When to hand off vs. do it yourself

| Situation | Hand off? |
|---|---|
| Need a result to continue (engineer builds the spec → reviewer verdicts) | **Yes — subagent** |
| Parallel independent read-only work | **Yes — multiple subagents in one reply** |
| Quick research / investigation / planning by another persona | **Yes** |
| Small task clearly inside your own role | **No — just do it** |
| Fire-and-forget | **Not an option** — no queue, call and wait |
| Multi-turn back-and-forth with the subagent | **No** — split into one-shot calls with full context each time |

## Writing prompts for subagents

1. **State the goal.** What outcome do you want back?
2. **Give the context.** File paths, excerpts, originating request, prior
   decisions. Paste the text — don't just reference it.
3. **Set the constraints.** Format, length, scope, what *not* to do.
4. **Bound the response.** "Report in under 200 words." "Return the Run
   Report only." "List files as a bullet list with one-line annotations."

Facts, not diplomacy: a reviewer's findings go back to the builder as
written, and a builder's blockers go back to the reviewer as written — the
value of a separate slot is its unsoftened judgment. Terse prompts produce
shallow, generic work. Be specific or don't hand off.

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't hand off trivially.** One grep and one edit away? Do it.
- **Don't hand off to a persona not in the roster above.** It's a hard
  error — check the roster first.
- **Don't write a dispatch as text.** Only a call to your subagent tool
  runs anything; prose and pasted syntax from another host both print and
  do nothing.
- **Don't edit agent frontmatter to "enable" dispatch.** Nothing needs
  enabling; on Copilot a `tools:` key can only take tools away, and
  `handoffs:` is post-run navigation, not an in-run subagent call.
- **Don't hand off and discard.** The subagent's result belongs in your
  reply. Silent discards are lost work.
- **Don't try to simulate async.** There is no queue. Call, wait, continue.

## Reporting back to your caller

The subagent's result is yours to integrate — don't narrate the tool
calls, show the outcome. After a hand-off, summarize what each subagent
produced, show the concrete deliverable, and call out blockers and next
steps in the same reply.
```
